status_summary: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644, Public Law 119-101) became law on 2026-07-11 without the President's signature; its Section 107 directs HUD to publish nonbinding zoning frameworks and bars adverse HUD action against localities that decline them, and Section 208 creates an Innovation Fund authorized at 200 million dollars a year for FY2027 through FY2031 that rewards housing supply growth while stating that HUD gains no power to mandate, supersede or preempt local zoning. Per CRS, Section 213 cuts CDBG allocations by 10 percent from FY2029 for entitlement communities with below-median housing growth improvement, which adds federal fiscal pressure on local land use. Executive Order 14394 (published 2026-03-18) directed HUD to issue voluntary best practices, including by-right single-family development, without preempting local authority, and HUD withdrew a 2016 joint statement on land use law and the Fair Housing Act in a notice published 2026-07-17. Executive Order 14438 of 2026-10-22 (91 FR 68007) directs a new manufactured housing task force to evaluate conditioning federal grants on state and local adoption of standardized permitting, a study step that preempts no local authority.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14394 was published, directing HUD to issue voluntary state and local best practices on housing regulation, including by-right single-family development.
The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644) became law as Public Law 119-101 without the President's signature.
HUD published a notice withdrawing guidance documents including a 2016 joint statement on land use law and the Fair Housing Act.

Executive Order 14438, Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People (signed 2026-10-22, published 2026-10-28 at 91 FR 68007), creates a Task Force on Manufactured Housing Innovation, co-chaired by HUD and FHFA with Agriculture, Commerce and Veterans Affairs, to recommend within 180 days ways to reduce federal requirements on factory-built housing, and directs it to evaluate whether federal grant funding may be conditioned on, or used to encourage, state and local adoption of standardized permitting and licensing for such housing, citing best practices issued under Executive Order 14394; it does not address zoning or preemption.

title: Oppose federal preemption of local zoning and defend single-family zoning
uncertainties: The enrolled text of Public Law 119-101 was read in review on govinfo.gov through Section 212 (Sections 107, 207 and 208 confirmed); the HTML, PDF and USLM copies all cut off before Section 213 in the fetch tool, so Section 213 rests on CRS R49354, which was read in its first 100,000 characters in review. Provisions such as Sections 103 and 206 were not examined for zoning effects beyond their headings. The HUD page titled State and Local Best Practices for Home Construction cites Executive Order 14394 and recommends by-right single-family development, but it carries no date, so it is not a dated timeline event; the order set a 60-day deadline of about 2026-05-12. The HUD withdrawal notice states an effective date of 2025-09-25, earlier than its publication. The classification is partial because the law avoids preemption but adds incentives and a CDBG adjustment that push toward zoning change. The 2026-10-22 executive order was published on 2026-10-28 as Executive Order 14438 (91 FR 68007 to 68009, FR Doc. 2026-22051) and was read in the GovInfo PDF; its permitting provisions concern manufactured and factory-built housing, and it does not mention zoning or preemption, so its bearing on local land use depends on what the task force recommends.
